x: Allen, Paddy Woods and our Bert Clayton with a disputed first place; Bert looked very comfortable and seemed quite willing to let the other two set the pace.

The absence of Dave McMullen and Gerry Gregory no doubt accounted for Surrey A.C.'s first scratch team win for many years, and with Paddy Woods narrowly beating Harry Churcher for individual honours, the Surrey boys are to be congratulated on their dual win.

The question of altering the course is now being seriously considered and it is hoped that we shall be able to avoid any such mishap in the future. As usual, we had a match with the Police and Paddy Woods, continuing his Imber Court form, just beat Harry into first place.

Immediately, from a fast start, Paddy Woods took the lead, surrounded by five members of the Sheffield team, obviously meaning business in the team race, but soon after the first mile post was passed two Sheffield lads were " pulled " and five of their men were out in the first four miles.
… thereafter there was no holding him, and he went through from the middle of the field to finish only 23 seconds behind Paddy Woods who had been in the lead all the way.…
Once again Harry Churcher was 1st in the Surrey two miles track race, having finished 2nd to Paddy Woods by a narrow margin in the Track Seven.

James and George Oliver could be seen leading the field, with Paddy Woods and George Checkley following close behind. Down the hill positions closed up and there were little packs of walkers together.

Surrey had four home with 25 points when suddenly Doub appeared in company with Paddy Woods. If Doub didn't come in first we should lose the team race, when for some reason, Paddy almost stopped to speak to someone, leaving Doub to go on and thus give us the victory.

Syd had Paddy Woods literally on his heels the whole way but did not let this disturb him. Youngsters, and new scoring members of our County team were Nick Milsum and Terry Clark who finished 8th and 10th respectively.
